evidence.title: Automatic Data Curation for Self-Supervised Learning: A Clustering-Based Approach
evidence.design: Successive hierarchical k-means on a large unlabeled pool, then hierarchical balanced sampling across cluster levels (sampling method r = resampling-based; flat = single-level). Curated set used to pretrain DINOv2-reg ViT-L.
evidence.dataset: Pool of ~743M images; curated sets ~100M images. Also satellite and text domains in the abstract. No dermatology.
evidence.baseline: Uncurated raw pool; flat sampling; random k-means init; manually curated ImageNet-1k and ImageNet-22k.
evidence.result: Full text, PARTIAL extraction. Table 3b (ViT-L, kNN ImageNet / ImageNet-val / in-A / sketch / iNat18 / iNat21 / Oxford-H retrieval): hierarchical '4r' 79.6 / 84.7 / 66.4 / 60.5 / 75.7 / 82.3 / 32.1 vs flat '4r-flat' 78.9 / 84.4 / 64.6 / 59.2 / 74.6 / 81.5 / 18.3. Table 3c: k-means++ init 79.6 kNN vs random init 74.0 kNN (same other settings). Table 3a: raw pool kNN 73.6 vs 4r 79.6. Table 4 (vs base feature extractor): base kNN 81.3, in-A 38.8, sketch 34.7, iNat18 64.1, iNat21 71.6, Oxford-H 14.9 vs 4r kNN 79.6, in-A 66.4, sketch 60.5, iNat18 75.7, iNat21 82.3, Oxford-H 32.1.
evidence.which_class: Not per-class. Long-tailed proxy = iNaturalist 2018/2021 (fine-grained, long-tailed), not medical.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (tables 3-4 and sampling section 3.3 passages). Seed count not verified in extraction.
evidence.limitation: Scale: 743M-image pool and 100M curated set; our pool is ~2.7k images (HAM dev 1528 + PAD adapt 1134). Hierarchical k-means at our size yields few clusters and noisy partitions. Curated set underperforms base on ImageNet kNN (-1.7 pp). Gains on long-tail/retrieval are on natural images. Single-run ablation tables as far as extracted.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Directly targets our cluster sampler: our PhA (inverse cluster-size weighting) is the flat, alpha-weighted variant. Vo's hierarchical balanced sampling (uniform over clusters at each level, then uniform within) is a different, more principled sampler, and the flat-vs-hierarchical ablation (+0.7 kNN, +1.1 iNat18, +13.8 retrieval) is the closest evidence we have for it. Not measured in our brief.

evidence.title: ExPLoRA: Parameter-Efficient Extended Pre-Training to Adapt Vision Transformers under Domain Shifts
evidence.design: Initialize ViT from DINOv2 or MAE weights; continue the SSL objective on the new domain; unfreeze 1-2 ViT blocks (plus norms) and train all other layers with LoRA (rank r, on Q and V). Then supervised fine-tune with LoRA or linear probe.
evidence.dataset: Satellite imagery (fMoW-RGB and WILDS datasets). No dermatology.
evidence.baseline: DINOv2 ViT-L linear probe; domain-specific SSL FMs (SatMAE, ScaleMAE, etc.).
evidence.result: Full text, PARTIAL extraction. Table 2 linear probing fMoW-RGB: DinoV2 ViT-L 67.60 -> ExPLoRA D-[L]-r64 76.86 (+9.3 pp). The dagger rows (DinoV2 69.00 -> D-[L]-r64 77.48) are not defined in the extracted text. Text claims +8.2 pp linear probing on fMoW (inconsistent with the table difference; resolve against the PDF). Compute claim: ~100 GPU h vs 960+ h for full pretraining (author-reported).
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (abstract, intro, Table 1-2, ablation pointer). Ablation Table 3 not read.
evidence.limitation: Satellite domain shift is far larger than dermoscopy vs natural photos. Method reads as ~1-2 unfrozen blocks plus LoRA on frozen blocks; our setup already unfreezes blocks 8-11 with full weights, which is a close relative. The brief's freeze arm and L2-SP arm are negative, so an ExPLoRA variant is probably redundant with those results.
evidence.relevance_to_us: Our current arm is already ExPLoRA-like (unfrozen top blocks). The only new element is LoRA in frozen blocks 0-7 (extra adaptation capacity at low cost). Expected effect low; see experiment X3.

evidence.title: DINOv3
evidence.design: Scales DINOv2-style SSL to a 7B ViT. Adds Gram anchoring: a regularizer that matches patch-level cosine-similarity structure (Gram matrix) to an earlier, cleaner teacher, to stop dense-feature degradation during long training. Then high-resolution post-training stage and distillation to ViT-S/B/L and ConvNeXt variants.
evidence.dataset: Large web-scale image corpus (Meta, ~1.7B images per the DinoDental citation of DINOv3). Downstream: ADE20K, NYU depth, ImageNet, ObjectNet, DAVIS.
evidence.baseline: DINOv2 and the DINOv3 model before Gram anchoring (ablation table).
evidence.result: Full text, PARTIAL extraction. Gram ablation (Fig. 9b table): Baseline linear ImageNet 88.2 / ADE mIoU 50.3 / NYU RMSE 0.307; GRAM 200k x1: 88.0 / 53.6 / 0.285; GRAM 200k x2: 88.0 / 55.7 / 0.281. So Gram anchoring trades about 0.2 pp global linear accuracy for +3.3 to +5.4 mIoU and lower depth RMSE. High-resolution adaptation: linear, OOD, segmentation and DAVIS improve after resolution scaling (Fig. 11).
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (Sec. 4 passages, Fig. 9b table, Sec. 5 headings). Full training recipe not read.
evidence.limitation: Gram anchoring is designed for 7B-scale long schedules on web data. Its benefit for a 6000-step, 2.7k-image continued run is untested. The regularizer pulls toward the teacher, which is the same mechanism as the negative L2-SP arm.
evidence.relevance_to_us: The only label-free method in this set that directly targets dense-feature quality under continued training. Our brief has patch-level (cls4patch) readouts but no Gram-type regularizer. Expected effect on CLS4 readout is small (DINOv3 saw -0.2 pp linear); benefit would show mainly on patch-level endpoints. See X2.

evidence.title: MedDINOv3: How to adapt vision foundation models for medical image segmentation?
evidence.design: Adapts DINOv3 to CT segmentation: multi-scale token aggregation from intermediate blocks, then domain-adaptive pretraining on CT-3M (3.87M axial CT slices) in three stages: DINOv2-style self-distillation, Gram anchoring, high-resolution (896) stage.
evidence.dataset: CT-3M (16 CT datasets). Evaluation: AMOS22, BTCV, KiTS23, LiTS. Segmentation with nnU-Net framework.
evidence.baseline: Random-init ViT; DINOv3-init ViT; nnU-Net; other medical FMs.
evidence.result: Full text, PARTIAL extraction. Table 1 (AMOS22 DSC): random init 78.39 -> DINOv3 init 81.35 -> + multi-scale features 83.45 -> + 896 resolution 85.51. Ablation Table 3 (multi-stage pretraining): stage 1 (DINOv2-style) improves DSC by about 1.07 pts; the paper states Gram anchoring is optional in their setting.
evidence.fulltext_or_abstract: Full text, PARTIAL extraction (Table 1, Sec. 4.3 passages).
evidence.limitation: Segmentation, not classification with frozen readouts. CT, not dermoscopy. Single fold on some tasks (stated).
evidence.relevance_to_us: Strongest direct precedent for continued DINO-style SSL on a medical domain with a frozen-to-trainable ladder. It supports the high-res stage (which our 448 arm already partly tests) and makes Gram anchoring look optional, which lowers the priority of X2.

experiments_ranked.name: Vo 2024 hierarchical balanced sampler (replaces our flat cluster sampler)
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Replace the PhA flat inverse-cluster-size sampler with two-level hierarchical sampling. Every 5 epochs: encode the pool with the current query encoder (CLS4, pre-projection, L2), PCA to 128 dims, L2-normalize. Level 1: k-means++ (n_init=3, fixed seed) with K1 about 50 (average top cluster size about 53 at N=2662). Level 2: inside each top cluster run k-means with K2 about 5 (average leaf size about 10). Sample a top cluster uniformly, then a leaf uniformly, then an image uniformly. The MoCo queue, key encoder and loss are unchanged. Use k-means++ init, not random (Vo Table 3c). Log leaf-size histogram and the fraction in the largest top cluster.
experiments_ranked.why: Vo 2024 shows hierarchical sampling beats flat sampling on the same pool (ViT-L, kNN 79.6 vs 78.9; iNat18 75.7 vs 74.6; Oxford-H retrieval 32.1 vs 18.3) and that k-means++ matters (79.6 vs 74.0 kNN). Our PhA uses flat alpha weighting. Uniform-over-clusters at each level is a different balance rule and has direct evidence, unlike PhA.
experiments_ranked.arms: A: uniform (already measured, baseline). B: PhA alpha=0.5 (cluster-size weighting, from imbalance research). C: X1 hierarchical-uniform. Seeds 42/43/44, 224 px, 1 view. Compare every arm against a baseline refit in the same environment. Endpoints per the brief: HAM mel recall and mel->NV; PAD MEL recall, SCC recall, SCC->BCC; per-class precision and recall; seed-wise deltas.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Small to moderate. Subjective probability about 30% of a seed-consistent melanoma-recall gain with macro-F1 non-decreasing; about 60% chance of no change beyond seed noise. Large SCC gain (>3 pp) unlikely.
experiments_ranked.cost: CPU k-means on about 2.7k x 128 for two levels, seconds. One forward pass over the pool every 5 epochs (GPU0, under 1 min estimated, to verify). No extra training FLOPs. Compute is negligible versus training.
experiments_ranked.risk: (1) Top-level clusters may encode acquisition (ISIC vs PAD device, rulers, vignetting). Run the brief's offline NMI check against acquisition metadata first; discard the arm if NMI is high. (2) At N=2.7k, k-means partitions are unstable: require ARI >= 0.5 between two seeds, as in PhA. (3) Oversampling small leaves amplifies noise. (4) Overlaps with PhA (same family): run as a replacement for PhA arm B, not stacked on it, to avoid a double count.
experiments_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate for the mechanism (E1 full text, partial extraction, large pool). Low for transfer to dermoscopy at 2.7k images.

experiments_ranked.name: Backbone fork: continue DINOv3 ViT-B (distilled) instead of DINOv2 ViT-B/14
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Same MoCo continued-pretraining recipe, but initialized from the public distilled DINOv3 ViT-B weights (full text confirms ViT-S/B/L distilled variants exist). Patch size, embedding dim, input resolution and token count will likely change vs ViT-B/14; verify before any run. Requires a new baseline of the frozen-readout pipeline.
experiments_ranked.why: DINOv3 reports better dense features and robustness than DINOv2 (E3); DinoDental and FetalUS show DINOv3 is competitive on medical image tasks (abstract-level evidence). Starting point matters more than the SSL hyperparameters the brief has already exhausted.
experiments_ranked.arms: A: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 continued (current, measured). B: DINOv3 ViT-B continued with the same trainable-block ladder. Frozen-readout protocol unchanged. Seeds 42/43/44 for encoder; same-environment baseline refit for both.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Uncertain. Subjective about 35% chance of macro-F1 change greater than 0.5 pp in either direction; direction unknown a priori.
experiments_ranked.cost: Full new SSL run per seed (6000 steps each) on GPU0, plus new variant features and readouts. Highest cost of the list (several GPU hours per seed, to verify on the cluster). Needs a new baseline set.
experiments_ranked.risk: Breaks comparability with every historical arm in the brief. Architecture or patch-size change may invalidate the blocks 8-11 trainable ladder. This is a real fork (backbone choice). Present to project owner with the trade-off: keep DINOv2 for comparability, or spend compute to test DINOv3 as a new base.
experiments_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate for DINOv3 vs DINOv2 dense features (E3, full text partial). Low for dermoscopy outcomes (no direct derm evidence in this set).

experiments_ranked.name: Gram-anchoring patch regularizer against the frozen initial DINOv2 teacher
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Add a term L_gram = lambda * || G_student - G_teacher ||_F^2 / N^2 on L2-normalized patch tokens (G = patch-cosine Gram matrix). Teacher = frozen initial DINOv2 ViT-B/14 (no labels). Start lambda in {0.05, 0.1}, chosen by a fixed rule on the SSL loss curve, not on held-out tasks. Apply at 224 px only (high-res Gram is a separate arm).
experiments_ranked.why: DINOv3 shows Gram anchoring keeps dense features clean during long training (E3: ADE mIoU 50.3 -> 53.6 with linear accuracy -0.2 pp). Our brief has patch-level readouts but no regularizer targeting patch structure. MedDINOv3 (E4) found Gram anchoring optional, so the gain is uncertain.
experiments_ranked.arms: A: current (baseline). B: + L_gram lambda 0.05. C: + L_gram lambda 0.1. Seeds 42/43/44. Endpoints as in brief; add the cls4patch readout as a secondary endpoint.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Small on CLS4 readout (about 25% chance of a macro-F1 gain above 0.5 pp). Possible gain on patch-level readouts (about 40%). Mechanism is close to the negative L2-SP arm, so expect a trade-off, not a clear win.
experiments_ranked.cost: One extra frozen teacher forward per step (no backward through teacher). Roughly +25-35% per-step time (estimate; to measure). No new data.
experiments_ranked.risk: Pulling toward the initial DINOv2 may replicate the negative L2-SP and freeze arms, reducing domain adaptation. Watch the mel->NV and SCC->BCC endpoints for a loss of adaptation.
experiments_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate for mechanism (E3, DINOv3 full text partial). Low for our task (E4 says optional).

experiments_ranked.name: ExPLoRA-style LoRA on the frozen blocks 0-7 (extra adaptation capacity)
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Keep blocks 8-11 fully trainable as now. Add LoRA (rank r=8, on Q and V) to blocks 0-7 with base weights frozen; train LoRA and LayerNorm in all blocks. Same MoCo loss, queue, schedule and 6000 steps.
experiments_ranked.why: ExPLoRA (E2) continues SSL with LoRA on frozen blocks and unfrozen top blocks; reports strong linear-probe gains on a far larger domain shift (satellite). Our setup is close but has no LoRA on lower blocks.
experiments_ranked.arms: A: current (baseline). B: + LoRA r=8 on blocks 0-7. Seeds 42/43/44. Endpoints as in brief.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Low. About 15% chance of a macro-F1 gain above 0.5 pp. Likely near the freeze and L2-SP arms, which are already negative.
experiments_ranked.cost: Low. Small added parameter count, similar compute to baseline. Needs a LoRA module in the encoder.
experiments_ranked.risk: High redundancy with tested negatives (freeze, L2-SP). Adds a hyperparameter (rank, alpha). Low expected information value; run only if X1 and X2 are flat.
experiments_ranked.evidence_strength: Moderate for the mechanism in satellite (E2, partial extraction). Low for dermoscopy.

experiments_ranked.name: Static frozen-teacher masked-latent prediction (SALT-style) as an extra loss
experiments_ranked.exact_change: Add a masked-patch latent prediction head: a student predictor regresses the frozen initial DINOv2 patch features at masked positions. Teacher is static (not EMA). Loss weight small, added to the MoCo loss.
experiments_ranked.why: US-JEPA (E5) reports that a static teacher gives stable latent targets and competitive linear-probe results on ultrasound. It differs from the EMA teacher listed as negative in the brief.
experiments_ranked.arms: A: current. B: + masked latent loss with static teacher. Seeds 42/43/44.
experiments_ranked.expected_effect: Low to uncertain. About 15% chance of a macro-F1 gain above 0.5 pp. Abstract-only evidence.
experiments_ranked.cost: Medium to high. New predictor and masking code; extra forward through the teacher; extra hyperparameters (mask ratio, loss weight).
experiments_ranked.risk: Abstract-only evidence. Implementation risk high for the time budget. Possible conflict with the MoCo contrastive loss.
